request.query: A linear map that fixes every polynomial is the identity; reconstruct polynomial as sum of monomials

content.text:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "LinearMap.toMvPolynomial_id",
      "informal_name": "Identity Linear Map Converts to Polynomial $X$",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} {M₁ : Type u_2} {ι₁ : Type u_4} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M₁] [inst_2 : Module R M₁]\n  [inst_3 : Fintype ι₁] [inst_4 : DecidableEq ι₁] (b₁ : Module.Basis ι₁ R M₁),\n  LinearMap.toMvPolynomial b₁ b₁ LinearMap.id = MvPolynomial.X",
      "informal_description": "The identity linear map on a module, when converted to a multivariate polynomial using the same basis for both domain and codomain, results in the polynomial variable $X$ representing the corresponding basis element.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Module.LinearMap.Polynomial"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.sum_monomial_eq",
      "informal_name": "Sum of Monomials Equals Polynomial",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R), (p.sum fun n a => (Polynomial.monomial n) a) = p",
      "informal_description": "For any polynomial $ p $ in $ R[X] $, the sum of the monomials $ a_n X^n $, where $ a_n $ are the coefficients of $ p $ and $ n $ ranges over the support of $ p $ (i.e., exponents with non-zero coefficients), equals $ p $ itself.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Basic"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.lsum_apply",
      "informal_name": "Linear Sum Application on Polynomial Coefficients",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M]\n  [inst_3 : Module R A] [inst_4 : Module R M] (f : ℕ → A →ₗ[R] M) (p : Polynomial A),\n  (Polynomial.lsum f) p = p.sum fun x1 x2 => (f x1) x2",
      "informal_description": "For semirings $ R $ and $ A $, an $ R $-module $ M $, and a family of $ R $-linear maps $ f_n : A \to M $ indexed by $ \\mathbb{N} $, applying the $ R $-linear map $ \\text{lsum}(f) $ to a polynomial $ p \\in A[X] $ yields the sum over all terms of $ f_n(a_n) $, where $ a_n $ is the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $. This operation preserves addition and scalar multiplication, ensuring linearity.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Coeff"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Polynomial.toFinsuppIsoLinear",
      "informal_name": "Linear Isomorphism between Polynomial Ring and Finitely Supported Functions on ℕ",
      "kind": "definition",
      "type": "(R : Type u) → [inst : Semiring R] → Polynomial R ≃ₗ[R] AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ",
      "informal_description": "The linear isomorphism between the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ and the additive monoid algebra $ R[\\mathbb{N}] $, constructed via the finitely supported function representation. This equivalence preserves both ring operations and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $, mapping each polynomial to its representation as a finitely supported function $ \\mathbb{N} \\to R $ and vice versa, with compositions yielding identity maps.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Basic"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "PolynomialLaw.id",
      "informal_name": "Identity Polynomial Law on an R-Module",
      "kind": "definition",
      "type": "{R : Type u} →\n  [inst : CommSemiring R] → {M : Type u_1} → [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : Module R M] → M →ₚₗ[R] M",
      "informal_description": "The identity polynomial law from an $ R $-module $ M $ to itself, defined by the identity function $ \text{id}_M $ that maps each element of $ M $ to itself. This is the polynomial law analogue of the identity map in the category of $ R $-modules.",
      "path": "Mathlib.RingTheory.PolynomialLaw.Basic"
    }
  ]
}

items.informal_name: Identity Linear Map Converts to Polynomial $X$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M₁ : Type u_2} {ι₁ : Type u_4} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M₁] [inst_2 : Module R M₁]
  [inst_3 : Fintype ι₁] [inst_4 : DecidableEq ι₁] (b₁ : Module.Basis ι₁ R M₁),
  LinearMap.toMvPolynomial b₁ b₁ LinearMap.id = MvPolynomial.X
items.informal_description: The identity linear map on a module, when converted to a multivariate polynomial using the same basis for both domain and codomain, results in the polynomial variable $X$ representing the corresponding basis element.

items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R), (p.sum fun n a => (Polynomial.monomial n) a) = p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in $ R[X] $, the sum of the monomials $ a_n X^n $, where $ a_n $ are the coefficients of $ p $ and $ n $ ranges over the support of $ p $ (i.e., exponents with non-zero coefficients), equals $ p $ itself.

items.informal_name: Linear Sum Application on Polynomial Coefficients
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_3 : Module R A] [inst_4 : Module R M] (f : ℕ → A →ₗ[R] M) (p : Polynomial A),
  (Polynomial.lsum f) p = p.sum fun x1 x2 => (f x1) x2
items.informal_description: For semirings $ R $ and $ A $, an $ R $-module $ M $, and a family of $ R $-linear maps $ f_n : A 	o M $ indexed by $ \mathbb{N} $, applying the $ R $-linear map $ \text{lsum}(f) $ to a polynomial $ p \in A[X] $ yields the sum over all terms of $ f_n(a_n) $, where $ a_n $ is the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $. This operation preserves addition and scalar multiplication, ensuring linearity.

items.informal_name: Linear Isomorphism between Polynomial Ring and Finitely Supported Functions on ℕ
items.type: (R : Type u) → [inst : Semiring R] → Polynomial R ≃ₗ[R] AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ
items.informal_description: The linear isomorphism between the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ and the additive monoid algebra $ R[\mathbb{N}] $, constructed via the finitely supported function representation. This equivalence preserves both ring operations and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $, mapping each polynomial to its representation as a finitely supported function $ \mathbb{N} \to R $ and vice versa, with compositions yielding identity maps.

items.informal_name: Identity Polynomial Law on an R-Module
items.type:
{R : Type u} →
  [inst : CommSemiring R] → {M : Type u_1} → [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : Module R M] → M →ₚₗ[R] M
items.informal_description: The identity polynomial law from an $ R $-module $ M $ to itself, defined by the identity function $ 	ext{id}_M $ that maps each element of $ M $ to itself. This is the polynomial law analogue of the identity map in the category of $ R $-modules.
